components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
口 (mouth) — 吃 relates to eating, done with the mouth
乞 (qǐ) gives a sound close to 吃's reading chī
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
忄 (heart) — 惊 relates to an emotional reaction of shock or fright
京 (jīng) gives the sound — an exact match with 惊's reading jīng

example.hanzi: 听到那个消息,他大吃一惊。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào nàge xiāoxi, tā dà chī yī jīng.
example.english: Hearing that news, he was astounded.
example.fact: The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa produced a sound so loud it ruptured eardrums 40 miles away and was heard as far as 3,000 miles away in Australia — one of the loudest sounds ever recorded in human history. Sailors caught in the shockwave were astounded to see the sky turn pitch black at midday, and the blast triggered tsunamis that killed tens of thousands of people along the surrounding coasts.

components.note: 长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.
木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'

example.hanzi: 他的长相很像他父亲。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhǎngxiàng hěn xiàng tā fùqīn.
example.english: His appearance closely resembles his father's.
example.fact: Studies of identical twins raised apart show that facial appearance is among the most heritable human traits, with genetics accounting for the large majority of variation in features like nose shape and jawline. Researchers have even found that subtle habits tied to appearance, such as a particular smile or squint, can run in families across generations.

components.note: 足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.

易 has been interpreted two ways by paleographers: an early picture of a lizard or chameleon, whose color-changing skin gave the character its meaning 'to change'; or a hand pouring liquid from one vessel into another, tied to the same idea of exchange. Either reading treats 易 as a single indivisible pictograph rather than a compound of separate parts.

example.hanzi: 路易十四统治法国长达七十二年。
example.pinyin: Lùyì Shísì tǒngzhì Fàguó chángdá qīshí'èr nián.
example.english: Louis XIV ruled France for seventy-two years.
example.fact: Louis XIV of France reigned for 72 years and 110 days, the longest confirmed reign of any monarch in European history. He transformed a modest hunting lodge at Versailles into a palace of over 2,300 rooms, and the rigid daily rituals of his court set the standard for European royal etiquette for generations afterward.

components.note: 匕 (a person), doubled and mirrored — two people standing back-to-back; this shape was later reused to write the unrelated directional meaning 'north.'
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).

example.hanzi: 挪威北部经常能看到北极光。
example.pinyin: Nuówēi běibù jīngcháng néng kàndào běijíguāng.
example.english: The northern part of Norway often has views of the aurora borealis.
example.fact: The aurora borealis occurs when charged particles from the sun collide with gases roughly 100 to 300 kilometers up in Earth's atmosphere, exciting oxygen and nitrogen atoms until they release light. Oxygen typically produces the green and red hues, while nitrogen creates blue and purple, which is why the sky over far-northern towns can shift color within seconds.

components.note: 米 (grain, especially husked rice) — 精's meaning 'refined, essence, spirit' relates to rice refined to its purest form.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 精 is pronounced jīng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 这座花园是园丁精心设计的。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò huāyuán shì yuándīng jīngxīn shèjì de.
example.english: This garden was meticulously designed by the gardener.
example.fact: The rock garden at Ryōan-ji temple in Kyoto contains only fifteen stones arranged across a bed of raked white gravel, yet from any spot on the viewing veranda at least one stone is always hidden from sight. Historians still debate whether this was a deliberate design choice or simply a side effect of the garden's centuries of meticulous upkeep.

components.note: 无 is the simplified form of 無, whose ancient form pictured a person dancing with feathered or tasseled sleeves, likely depicting a ritual dance. That pictograph was borrowed for its sound to write the unrelated meaning 'without, not have,' and the original dance sense was eventually dropped entirely.
礻 (spirit, altar) — 礼 relates to ceremony and rites performed before the spirits.
乚 reflects the character's phonetic root, though its exact link to the modern reading lǐ is unclear today.

example.hanzi: 他对服务员说话很无礼。
example.pinyin: Tā duì fúwùyuán shuōhuà hěn wúlǐ.
example.english: He spoke very rudely to the waiter.
example.fact: Victorian etiquette manuals of the 1830s devoted entire chapters to the precise angle of a bow and the correct way to greet a stranger, treating even minor breaches as evidence of poor character. Many of these codes were designed less to promote genuine courtesy than to mark class boundaries, since only the wealthy had the leisure to memorize hundreds of such rules.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
钅 (metal/gold) — represents something valuable.
昔 (formerly, in the past) — valuable metal that has been mishandled or lost over time gave 错 its meaning 'mistake, wrong.'

example.hanzi: 这次事故不是他的过错。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì shìgù bú shì tā de guòcuò.
example.english: This accident was not his fault.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin in 1928 began with what he later called a careless mistake: he left a petri dish of bacteria uncovered while on vacation, and it became contaminated with mold. Rather than discard the ruined dish, he noticed the mold was killing the surrounding bacteria, a mishap that led directly to the first modern antibiotic.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恶 relates to an evil or malicious state of heart/mind
亚 (yà) gives a sound distantly related to 恶's reading è, having drifted apart over time
木 (wood) — 棍 names an object made of wood, a stick.
昆 (kūn) gives a sound close to gùn, sharing the same rhyme and a related initial.

example.hanzi: 电影里的那个恶棍最后被警察抓住了。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de nàge ègùn zuìhòu bèi jǐngchá zhuāzhù le.
example.english: The scoundrel in the movie was eventually caught by the police.
example.fact: Blackbeard, the English pirate Edward Teach, terrorized the Caribbean and American coast for only about two years before his death in 1718, yet he built his fearsome reputation largely through theatrics. He reportedly wove lit fuses into his beard during battle so that smoke curled around his face and made him look demonic to his victims.

components.note: 阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning settlement or region) ties 那 to its original use as the name of a place west of the Zhou kingdom.
冄 is close in sound to 那's original reading. Over time the character's use shifted from a specific place name to the common demonstrative meaning 'that.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

example.hanzi: 那年夏天特别热。
example.pinyin: Nà nián xiàtiān tèbié rè.
example.english: That summer was especially hot.
example.fact: 2023 was confirmed as the hottest year on record globally, with average surface temperatures about 1.45°C above pre-industrial levels. Scientists linked much of the extreme heat to a strong El Niño event, a periodic shift that moves vast amounts of stored heat from the Pacific Ocean into the atmosphere.

components.note: 大 (a person) at the top represents someone leading.
冖 (a rope or cover shape) in the middle shows a tether.
牛 (ox) at the bottom is the animal being led, giving 牵 its meaning 'to lead by hand, to pull.'
氵 (water/stream) — the water being crossed.
步 (to step, walk) — feet moving through it, together giving 涉 its meaning 'to wade across' and, more broadly, 'to be involved in.'

example.hanzi: 这个案子牵涉到好几个国家。
example.pinyin: Zhège ànzi qiānshè dào hǎo jǐ gè guójiā.
example.english: This case involves several countries.
example.fact: The 2016 Panama Papers leak involved more than 11.5 million documents from a single Panamanian law firm and implicated politicians, business leaders, and celebrities from over 200 countries and territories. It remains one of the largest data leaks in journalism history, compiled by more than 100 media organizations working together for over a year before publication.

components.note: 阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning settlement or region) ties 那 to its original use as the name of a place west of the Zhou kingdom.
冄 is close in sound to 那's original reading. Over time the character's use shifted from a specific place name to the common demonstrative meaning 'that.'
段 shows 殳 (a hand wielding a tool) cutting or shaping stone into pieces — giving 段 its meaning 'section, segment, paragraph.'

example.hanzi: 那段时间他每天都在图书馆学习。
example.pinyin: Nà duàn shíjiān tā měitiān dōu zài túshūguǎn xuéxí.
example.english: During that period, he studied at the library every day.
example.fact: When Cambridge University closed because of the plague in 1665 and 1666, Isaac Newton spent nearly two years working alone at his family's farm in Woolsthorpe. During that stretch, later called his 'annus mirabilis,' he laid the groundwork for calculus, the theory of gravity, and his early work on optics.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 激 originally described water dashing or surging forcefully
敫 (jiǎo) gives a sound distantly related to 激's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
心 (heart) — 怒 relates to strong feeling in the heart: anger.
奴 (nú) gives a sound close to nù, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 他的话激怒了在场的所有人。
example.pinyin: Tā de huà jīnù le zàichǎng de suǒyǒu rén.
example.english: His words infuriated everyone present.
example.fact: In December 1773, a new British tax on tea infuriated colonists in Boston so much that a group calling themselves the Sons of Liberty boarded three ships and dumped 342 chests of tea into the harbor. The tea, worth roughly $1.7 million in today's money, took weeks to wash ashore up and down the New England coast.

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
东 (simplified from 東) originally pictured the sun 日 rising behind a tree 木 — since the sun rises in the east, the character came to mean 'east.'
尸 (a seated or reclining figure) forms the upper portion, picturing a person.

匕 (a person turned to face the other way) sits beneath, giving 尼 its early sense 'to draw near, to stop.' The character was later borrowed purely for its sound, both in Buddhist terms like 尼姑 (nun) and in phonetic transliterations of foreign names.

example.hanzi: 安东尼是我们班新来的交换生。
example.pinyin: Āndōngní shì wǒmen bān xīn lái de jiāohuànshēng.
example.english: Anthony is the new exchange student in our class.
example.fact: The Roman general Mark Antony formed a political and romantic alliance with Cleopatra of Egypt that ultimately clashed with Octavian's forces at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC. His defeat there marked the end of the Roman Republic's civil wars and the beginning of the Roman Empire under Augustus.

components.note: 太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'
平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
氵 (water) — 洋 refers to the vast ocean
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 洋's reading yáng

example.hanzi: 太平洋是世界上最大的海洋。
example.pinyin: Tàipíng Yáng shì shìjiè shàng zuì dà de hǎiyáng.
example.english: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean in the world.
example.fact: The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square kilometers, more than all of Earth's land area combined. Its deepest point, the Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep, plunges nearly 11,000 meters below the surface — deep enough to submerge Mount Everest with room to spare.

components.note: 高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
层 depicts a roof-like covering stacked over what lies beneath, evoking one layer piled upon another.

example.hanzi: 这座城市有很多高层建筑。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu hěn duō gāocéng jiànzhù.
example.english: This city has many high-rise buildings.
example.fact: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai stands 828 meters tall, making it the world's tallest building since it opened in 2010. Its design was inspired by the geometric patterns of a desert flower called the Hymenocallis, and the building's spire alone is taller than the Eiffel Tower.

meanings: younger male cousin through a female relative

components.note: 毛 (fur, hair) — 表 originally pictured a fur garment worn on the outside.
衣 (clothing) — an outer fur wrap gave 表 its meaning of 'outer' or 'surface,' and later, 'to express' (showing something on the surface).

弟 originally pictured a wooden stake wrapped with cord wound around it in even, successive turns, evoking the idea of order or sequence. That sense of 'in order, one after another' extended naturally to 'younger brother,' the sibling who comes after in birth order.

example.hanzi: 我表弟比我小三岁。
example.pinyin: Wǒ biǎodì bǐ wǒ xiǎo sān suì.
example.english: My cousin is three years younger than me.
example.fact: Queen Victoria and Prince Albert, who married in 1840, were first cousins — a common practice among European royalty at the time meant to keep power within extended families. Geneticists later linked this same practice to the spread of hemophilia through several royal houses of Europe, traced back to Victoria herself.

components.note: 口 (mouths) — 总 pictures many voices.
心 (heart, mind) — many mouths brought together under one mind gave 总 its meaning 'overall' or 'to gather together.'
八 (a hand shape) — one of two hands shown reaching toward the same object.
廾 (two hands together) — jointly holding up one object, giving 共 its meaning 'together, joint, common.'

example.hanzi: 这次旅行总共花了三千块钱。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng zǒnggòng huā le sānqiān kuài qián.
example.english: This trip cost three thousand yuan altogether.
example.fact: A 2012 archaeological survey found that the Great Wall of China, counting all its branches and sections built across different dynasties, measures 21,196 kilometers altogether — more than four times earlier estimates that only counted the best-preserved Ming-era sections.

components.note: 亻 (a person) shows a human figure at the center of the character's original meaning.
可 is close in sound to 何's reading hé. The combined character first meant 'to carry on the shoulder,' a person bearing a load on a pole, before being borrowed for the interrogative 'what, which.'
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'

example.hanzi: 他不知道自己身在何处。
example.pinyin: Tā bù zhīdào zìjǐ shēn zài héchù.
example.english: He didn't know where he was.
example.fact: Amelia Earhart's final radio transmission on July 2, 1937, reported that she and navigator Fred Noonan did not know where they were, running low on fuel somewhere near Howland Island in the Pacific. Despite one of the largest search efforts in U.S. history at the time, the wreckage of her plane has never been conclusively found.

components.note: 虫 (worm, insect) — 蠢 originally described the wriggling movement of insects.
春 (chūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 蠢, differing only in tone.

事 depicts a hand at the bottom gripping a forked instrument or ceremonial banner at the top, an image originally tied to holding an official post or duty. From that sense of an official's charge, 事 broadened to mean any 'matter, affair, or thing that happens.'

example.hanzi: 年轻时谁没做过几件蠢事呢?
example.pinyin: Niánqīng shí shéi méi zuòguò jǐ jiàn chǔnshì ne?
example.english: Who hasn't done a few foolish things when they were young?
example.fact: When U.S. Secretary of State William Seward negotiated the purchase of Alaska from Russia in 1867 for $7.2 million, newspapers mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly,' certain the frozen territory was worthless. Just thirty years later, the Klondike Gold Rush and later oil discoveries proved the acquisition to be one of the most valuable land deals in American history.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.
讠 (speech) — 语 relates to language, words, and speech
吾 (wú) gives a loose sound connection to 语's reading yǔ

example.hanzi: 她在大学里学了四年德语。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué lǐ xué le sì nián Déyǔ.
example.english: She studied German for four years in university.
example.fact: German is the most widely spoken native language in the European Union, with over 95 million native speakers — more than French, Italian, or Spanish. It is also known for compound nouns of startling length, such as a 39-letter word once used in actual German legal texts to mean 'legal protection insurance companies.'

components.note: 囗 (an enclosure) — something firmly closed in is secure, tied to 固's meaning 'solid, firm.'
古 (gǔ) gives a rhyme close to gù, with the tone shifted.
扌 (hand) — a hand gripping something tightly
丸 (a pebble/pellet) — the small object held firmly in the hand

example.hanzi: 老人固执地拒绝去医院看病。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén gùzhí de jùjué qù yīyuàn kànbìng.
example.english: The old man stubbornly refused to go to the hospital.
example.fact: Mules are proverbially called stubborn, but animal behaviorists note their caution is really a survival trait: unlike horses, mules assess a risky situation, like an unstable bridge or unfamiliar footing, before committing, and will simply refuse to move if they judge it unsafe. That trait has kept many riders out of danger over the centuries.

components.note: 文 depicts a chest marked with crossing lines, once tattoos or patterns on the body — decoration and pattern gave rise to the idea of 'writing' and 'culture.'
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.

example.hanzi: 她大学主修中国文学。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué zhǔxiū Zhōngguó wénxué.
example.english: She majored in Chinese literature in college.
example.fact: Murasaki Shikibu's 'The Tale of Genji,' written in Japan around the year 1000 AD, is widely considered the world's first psychological novel. It runs to more than 1,100 pages in translation and follows over 400 characters across generations of a single imperial family.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 摄 describes taking hold of or capturing something, as in taking a photograph.
聂 (niè) gives a sound distantly related to shè's reading, having drifted apart over time.
彡 (fine lines) — suggests light and shadow, relating to 影's meaning 'shadow, image.'
景 (jǐng) gives a sound hint — 影 is pronounced yǐng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.

example.hanzi: 剧组带来了三台摄影机拍摄这场戏。
example.pinyin: Jùzǔ dàilái le sān tái shèyǐngjī pāishè zhè chǎng xì.
example.english: The crew brought three movie cameras to film this scene.
example.fact: The Lumière brothers' Cinématographe, first demonstrated publicly in Paris in December 1895, could both film and project movies using the same hand-cranked device. Their very first films, like a fifty-second clip of workers leaving a factory, are considered among the earliest true motion pictures ever shown to a paying audience.

components.note: 才 (talent) — many talented people.
囗 (an enclosure) — gathered together in one place, giving 团 its meaning 'group, team; round, ball-shaped.'
亻 (person) — 伙 relates to people who share meals or work together.
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 伙's reading huǒ.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了一个盗窃团伙。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔ le yī gè dàoqiè tuánhuǒ.
example.english: The police arrested a theft gang.
example.fact: The Great Train Robbery of August 1963 saw a gang of fifteen men steal £2.6 million, worth well over £50 million today, from a Royal Mail train in Buckinghamshire, England. Ironically, part of the gang's downfall came from a rented farmhouse hideout where investigators later found their fingerprints on a Monopoly board they had used to pass the time.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — 冷 relates to the cold of ice
令 (lìng) gives a sound close to 冷's reading lěng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
Wine — the original sense described the strong taste of wine.
Gives the sound gào, related to kù but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他对朋友的困境表现得很冷酷。
example.pinyin: Tā duì péngyǒu de kùnjìng biǎoxiàn de hěn lěngkù.
example.english: He was quite callous about his friend's difficulties.
example.fact: The 1964 murder of Kitty Genovese in New York City became a landmark case in social psychology after newspaper reports claimed dozens of neighbors heard her cries but did nothing to help. Although later research showed the original account was exaggerated, the case still gave rise to the term 'bystander effect,' describing how people become less likely to intervene the more witnesses are present.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'

example.hanzi: 我们一同去看了那场电影。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yītóng qù kàn le nà chǎng diànyǐng.
example.english: We went to see that movie together.
example.fact: James Watson and Francis Crick worked together at Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratory to determine the double-helix structure of DNA, publishing their findings in a single one-page paper in Nature in April 1953. Their model relied heavily on X-ray diffraction images produced by their colleague Rosalind Franklin, whose contribution went largely unacknowledged at the time.

components.note: 广 (shelter) suggests a piece of furniture kept indoors.
木 (wood) — early beds were built from wood, giving 床 its meaning.

单 is the simplified form of 單, whose oracle-bone shape resembled a forked hunting weapon or a simple slingshot mounted on a handle — a tool wielded alone by a single hunter. That link to a solitary user is thought to have given 单 its later meaning 'single, sole, odd (number).'

example.hanzi: 妈妈每周都会换洗床单。
example.pinyin: Māma měi zhōu dōu huì huànxǐ chuángdān.
example.english: Mom changes and washes the bed sheets every week.
example.fact: A typical unwashed bed sheet can host hundreds of thousands of dust mites, microscopic creatures that feed on shed human skin cells and thrive in the warm, humid environment bedding provides. Their droppings are actually a leading cause of indoor allergies, which is why sleep specialists recommend washing sheets in hot water at least once a week.

components.note: 阝 (mound, place) shows 陪 relates to being present alongside someone somewhere.
咅 gives a sound distantly related to péi, having drifted apart over time.
宀 (roof) — 审 relates to a formal setting, like a courtroom, where matters are examined
申 (shēn) gives a sound close to 审's reading shěn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.hanzi: 他被选为这次审判的陪审员。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi xuǎn wéi zhè cì shěnpàn de péishěnyuán.
example.english: He was selected as a juror for this trial.
example.fact: The tradition of a twelve-person jury traces back to medieval England, though the reason for that specific number remains uncertain — some historians link it to the twelve apostles, others to earlier Anglo-Saxon legal customs. The right to trial by a jury of one's peers was formally enshrined in the Magna Carta of 1215.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
目 (eye) — 睁 describes an action of the eyes.
争 (zhēng) gives the sound — an exact match for 睁.
目 (eye) — 睁 describes an action of the eyes.
争 (zhēng) gives the sound — an exact match for 睁.

example.hanzi: 他眼睁睁地看着机会溜走,却无能为力。
example.pinyin: Tā yǎnzhēngzhēng de kànzhe jīhuì liūzǒu, què wúnéngwéilì.
example.english: He watched helplessly as the opportunity slipped away, powerless to stop it.
example.fact: When the airship Hindenburg caught fire while landing in New Jersey in 1937, ground crew and radio announcer Herbert Morrison watched helplessly as the hydrogen-filled vessel burned and crashed in just 34 seconds. The disaster, captured on newsreel film and narrated live on radio, effectively ended the era of passenger airship travel.

components.note: 王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.
木 (wood) recalls 查's early meaning: a raft of lashed logs used to ford a river or gauge its depth.

旦 matches the sound of chá's older reading and anchors the character phonetically, though the connection has drifted with later sound changes. From 'testing a river crossing,' 查 broadened to its modern sense 'to check, to investigate.'
心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.

example.hanzi: 理查德是这家公司的创始人之一。
example.pinyin: Lǐchádé shì zhè jiā gōngsī de chuàngshǐrén zhī yī.
example.english: Richard is one of the founders of this company.
example.fact: In 2012, archaeologists digging beneath a parking lot in Leicester, England, discovered the skeleton of King Richard III, who had died in battle in 1485. DNA testing confirmed the identity by comparing it to living descendants of his sister, and the skeleton's curved spine matched historical accounts describing the king's scoliosis.

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'

example.hanzi: 学习一门语言好比爬一座山,需要坚持不懈。
example.pinyin: Xuéxí yī mén yǔyán hǎobǐ pá yī zuò shān, xūyào jiānchí bùxiè.
example.english: Learning a language is just like climbing a mountain — it requires persistence.
example.fact: Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first climbers confirmed to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1953, after a British expedition of over 400 people, including porters, hauled nearly 18,000 pounds of supplies to base camp. Even today, roughly one in every hundred people who attempt the summit dies in the process.

components.note: 面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).

example.hanzi: 医生检查了病人的面部表情。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le bìngrén de miànbù biǎoqíng.
example.english: The doctor examined the patient's facial expressions.
example.fact: Psychologist Paul Ekman's research found that the human face has 43 individual muscles capable of combining into more than 10,000 distinct expressions, though only about 3,000 of these carry meaningful emotional significance. His work on universal facial expressions across cultures later inspired the animated emotions in Pixar's 'Inside Out.'

components.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
酋 pictures a jar of wine.
寸 (hand) below offers it up respectfully, giving 尊 its meaning 'to respect, to honor.'

example.hanzi: 每个人都应该保持自己的自尊。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yīnggāi bǎochí zìjǐ de zìzūn.
example.english: Everyone should maintain their own self-respect.
example.fact: Psychologist Abraham Maslow placed self-esteem near the top of his 1943 hierarchy of needs, arguing that people cannot pursue their fullest potential until more basic needs for safety, belonging, and respect are met. Later research has complicated this strict ordering, showing that people facing extreme poverty or danger can still report a strong sense of purpose and self-worth.

components.note: 穴 (hole/cave) — 窗 originally described an opening for light and air.
囱 (cōng) gives a sound distantly related to chuāng, having drifted apart over time.
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.

example.hanzi: 阳光透过窗口照进房间。
example.pinyin: Yángguāng tòuguò chuāngkǒu zhàojìn fángjiān.
example.english: Sunlight streams through the window into the room.
example.fact: Clear flat glass windows became affordable for ordinary homes only after the float glass process was invented by Alastair Pilkington in 1959, letting molten glass flow across a bed of liquid tin to form a perfectly smooth, undistorted sheet. Before this, most window glass had faint ripples that slightly warped the view.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 途 names a road or path traveled on.
余 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tú, having drifted apart over time.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

example.hanzi: 我们在途中遇到了一场大雨。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài túzhōng yùdào le yī chǎng dàyǔ.
example.english: We ran into a heavy rain while en route.
example.fact: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition set out in 1519 with five ships and about 270 men to circumnavigate the globe, but Magellan himself was killed in the Philippines partway through the voyage. Only one ship and 18 crew members survived to complete the full journey and return to Spain three years later.

components.note: 冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
贝 (shell/money) — 费 relates to spending money, fees, and expenses
弗 (fú) gives a loose sound connection to 费's reading fèi

example.hanzi: 这所大学的学费每年都在上涨。
example.pinyin: Zhè suǒ dàxué de xuéfèi měi nián dōu zài shàngzhǎng.
example.english: This university's tuition rises every year.
example.fact: Germany abolished tuition fees at public universities in 2014, making higher education essentially free even for international students, a policy rooted in the idea that education is a public good rather than a personal investment. By contrast, average tuition at a four-year private university in the United States that same year exceeded $30,000 per year.

components.note: 发 is the simplified form of 發, whose ancient shape combined a bow 弓 with two hands and a foot stepping down, picturing the act of shooting an arrow outward. That sense of 'sending something out' broadened over time into 'to issue, to emit, to develop' — the meaning carried in words like 发掘 (to excavate, to unearth).
扌 (hand) — 掘 describes digging with the hands or a tool.
屈 (qū) gives a sound distantly related to 掘's reading jué, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 考古学家在这里发掘出许多古代文物。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā zài zhèlǐ fājué chū xǔduō gǔdài wénwù.
example.english: Archaeologists excavated many ancient artifacts here.
example.fact: British archaeologist Howard Carter spent nearly five years searching the Valley of the Kings before he and his team finally excavated the largely intact tomb of Tutankhamun in November 1922. The tomb contained over 5,000 individual objects, including the pharaoh's iconic solid gold burial mask, and took nearly a decade to fully catalog and remove.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.

example.hanzi: 他到处打听那家餐厅的地址。
example.pinyin: Tā dàochù dǎting nà jiā cāntīng de dìzhǐ.
example.english: He asked around everywhere for that restaurant's address.
example.fact: Honeybee scouts that discover a good source of nectar perform a 'waggle dance' back at the hive, using the angle and duration of their movements to tell other bees the direction and distance to the flowers. Other bees essentially ask around by following and interpreting several dancing scouts before deciding where to fly.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
斗 depicts a hand-held dipper or ladle used for measuring grain and liquids — giving 斗 its meaning 'a unit of dry measure,' and by extension, the Big Dipper constellation.

example.hanzi: 两只狮子为了争夺地盘而打斗。
example.pinyin: Liǎng zhī shīzi wèile zhēngduó dìpán ér dǎdòu.
example.english: The two lions fought over territory.
example.fact: Male lions that take over a new pride will often fight to the death over territory, and a successful challenger frequently kills the cubs fathered by the previous male so that the pride's lionesses come back into estrus sooner. Roughly one in four male lion cubs dies from such conflicts before reaching adulthood.

components.note: 圣 is the simplified form of 聖, which combined an ear (耳, listening) and a mouth (口, speaking) above a standing figure — the image of someone who listens and speaks with special insight, giving 圣 its meaning 'holy, sacred.'
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'
哥 doubles the character 可 ('to approve, to sing'), originally suggesting a call-and-response song between two singers; the meaning later narrowed to 'elder brother.'

example.hanzi: 我们计划下个月去圣地亚哥旅游。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jìhuà xià gè yuè qù Shèngdìyàgē lǚyóu.
example.english: We're planning a trip to Santiago next month.
example.fact: Santiago, Chile, sits within one of the most seismically active regions on Earth, part of the Pacific Ring of Fire, and the country has recorded the strongest earthquake ever measured — a magnitude 9.5 event near Valdivia in 1960. Because of this constant risk, Chilean building codes are now among the strictest in the world.

components.note: 皿 (a vessel) — a chalice or bowl
丿 — a single drop of blood inside the vessel
⺼ (flesh/meat) — 腥 describes the strong smell of raw meat or fish.
星 (xīng) gives the sound — an exact match with 腥.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的场面十分血腥。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de chǎngmiàn shífēn xuèxīng.
example.english: The scenes in this movie are extremely bloody.
example.fact: The Battle of the Somme in 1916 remains one of the bloodiest single battles in human history: on its first day alone, British forces suffered about 57,000 casualties, nearly 20,000 of them fatal, making it the deadliest single day in the history of the British Army.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — 登 relates to climbing or ascending with one's legs
豆 (dòu) gives a sound distantly related to 登's reading dēng, having drifted apart over time

台 in the sense of 'platform, stage' is a simplified stand-in for the historically separate character 臺, whose ancient form pictured a tall building raised on an earthen mound — an elevated place for observation or ceremony. That original picture of a raised structure is the direct source of 登台's meaning 'to climb onto the stage.'

example.hanzi: 那位歌手第一次登台就赢得了满场喝彩。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi gēshǒu dìyī cì dēngtái jiù yíngdé le mǎnchǎng hècǎi.
example.english: That singer won thunderous applause the very first time she took the stage.
example.fact: When a 13-year-old Michael Jackson took the stage with his brothers at Harlem's Apollo Theater amateur night in 1967, the group's energetic performance reportedly caused the audience to erupt so loudly that the show's host had trouble restoring order. Their win that night helped launch the Jackson 5's professional career just two years later.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
囗 (an enclosure) — 四 pictures a bounded space.
儿 (a person) — a person enclosed within four walls gave 四 its meaning 'four,' though the exact link to the number is debated.

example.hanzi: 我们每星期四都有一次团队会议。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen měi Xīngqīsì dōu yǒu yī cì tuánduì huìyì.
example.english: We have a team meeting every Thursday.
example.fact: The English word 'Thursday' comes from 'Thor's day,' honoring the Norse god of thunder, a naming pattern the Anglo-Saxons borrowed when adapting the Roman calendar, which had named the same day after Jupiter, the Roman god associated with thunder and lightning.

components.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
艹 (plant) — the living thing in bloom.
化 (transformation) — the plant changing into blossom, the source of 花's meaning 'flower.'

example.hanzi: 电线短路时冒出了一串火花。
example.pinyin: Diànxiàn duǎnlù shí mào chū le yī chuàn huǒhuā.
example.english: A string of sparks shot out when the wire short-circuited.
example.fact: A single lightning bolt can heat the surrounding air to roughly 30,000 Kelvin, about five times hotter than the surface of the sun, all in a spark that typically lasts less than a millisecond. That rapid heating causes the air to expand explosively, producing the shockwave we hear as thunder.

meanings: (of a device, connection, material etc) defective

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

良 is thought to depict a granary building with a covered corridor for airing and drying grain, keeping it from spoiling. Grain properly aired this way stayed 'good, fine, sound' rather than rotting, which is likely the source of 良's core meaning.

example.hanzi: 长期熬夜会导致不良的健康后果。
example.pinyin: Chángqī áoyè huì dǎozhì bùliáng de jiànkāng hòuguǒ.
example.english: Long-term staying up late can lead to poor health consequences.
example.fact: Researchers at the University of California found that even a single night of significant sleep deprivation increases activity in the brain's amygdala, the region tied to emotional reactivity, while weakening its connection to the prefrontal cortex, which normally regulates that response. Chronic sleep loss has since been linked to measurable increases in the risk of heart disease, diabetes, and impaired immune function.

meanings: variant of 座標|坐标[zuo4 biao1]

components.note: 从 (two people, one following another) — depicts people together.
土 (earth/ground) — two people seated on the ground gave 坐 its meaning 'to sit.'
木 (wood/tree) — 标 originally referred to the tip of a tree, later coming to mean 'mark, sign'
票 (piào) gives a sound close to 标's reading biāo

example.hanzi: 飞行员输入了目的地的坐标。
example.pinyin: Fēixíngyuán shūrù le mùdìdì de zuòbiāo.
example.english: The pilot entered the coordinates of the destination.
example.fact: The Cartesian coordinate system, which lets any point on a plane be located using just two numbers, was introduced by French philosopher and mathematician René Descartes in 1637. Legend holds he was inspired by watching a fly crawl across the ceiling near his bed and realizing he could describe its position using its distance from two perpendicular walls.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 脚 refers to the foot, a part of the body
却 (què) gives a sound distantly related to 脚's reading jiǎo, having drifted apart over time
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 他小心地看着脚下的路,以免摔倒。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎoxīn de kànzhe jiǎoxià de lù, yǐmiǎn shuāidǎo.
example.english: He carefully watched the path under his feet so as not to fall.
example.fact: A single hectare of healthy soil can contain several tonnes of living organisms — bacteria, fungi, insects, and worms — quietly working underfoot to recycle nutrients. Scientists estimate that just one teaspoon of healthy soil can hold up to a billion bacterial cells, far more organisms than there are humans on Earth.

components.note: Flesh — skin is part of the body.
Gives the sound fū, matching the character's reading.
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'

example.hanzi: 阳光会让人的肤色变深。
example.pinyin: Yángguāng huì ràng rén de fūsè biàn shēn.
example.english: Sunlight makes a person's skin color darken.
example.fact: Human skin color evolved largely as a balance between two competing pressures: darker skin, rich in the pigment melanin, protects against UV-related DNA damage nearer the equator, while lighter skin allows more UV light to penetrate for vitamin D synthesis at higher latitudes with weaker sunlight. Genetic studies suggest this trait can shift within a population in as few as 100 generations under strong selective pressure.

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'

方 is generally read as a pictograph of an ancient plow blade, viewed from above with its handle and cutting edge. Because a plow cuts a straight, even furrow, the character came to represent 'square, straight, direction,' and later extended to 'a method' or 'a prescribed way of doing something' — the sense carried in 处方 (prescription).

example.hanzi: 医生给他开了一张处方。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi tā kāi le yī zhāng chǔfāng.
example.english: The doctor wrote him a prescription.
example.fact: The 'Rx' symbol used on medical prescriptions is widely believed to derive from the Latin word 'recipe,' meaning 'take,' though a popular but unproven legend traces it to the Eye of Horus, an ancient Egyptian protective symbol. The oldest known written prescriptions come from Mesopotamian clay tablets dating back over 4,000 years, listing plant- and mineral-based remedies for various ailments.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 苏 relates to certain aromatic plants and to reviving, coming back to life
稣 (sū) gives the sound — 苏 is also pronounced sū, an exact match
扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在饮料里加一点苏打水。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuān zài yǐnliào lǐ jiā yīdiǎn sūdá shuǐ.
example.english: He likes to add a little soda water to his drinks.
example.fact: English scientist Joseph Priestley invented a method for infusing water with carbon dioxide in 1767, creating the first artificial carbonated water, several years before he became famous for helping discover oxygen. His invention laid the groundwork for the entire soft drink industry, though it took decades before entrepreneurs began selling flavored versions commercially.
